solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A success in Treasure Island initially leads to another

indicators.note: in places the first group of letters within the pair of opening letters
initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: a success, as with a chart record, is a hit

explanation.surface: A lucky find on Stevenson's pirate island points the way to yet another island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: after Treasure Island, another island. 'initially' gives T and I, and 'in' places A HIT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is a South Pacific island, so after one island in the clue it is simply a further one.

clue.text: House shortlisted for demolition, it's not needed

indicators.note: for demolition says the letters of the first word are knocked down and rebuilt, with the letters of the word marked not needed left over

parts.note: the fodder whose letters are rearranged
these letters are the ones not needed, taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: A chamber of Parliament has been earmarked for abolition, since nobody needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of SHORTLISTED, minus I, T and S ('it's not needed'), rearranged give the answer. The surface echoes long talk of abolishing Britain's upper chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament, commonly called simply the Lords.

clue.text: Playing it on grass may be banned

definitions.text: Playing it on grass may be banned

parts.words: Playing it on grass may be banned
parts.note: playing suggests a sport on a grass pitch, but it is water played over a lawn, which British summer drought bans forbid

explanation.surface: A game on the turf might be outlawed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a dry British summer water companies impose 'hosepipe bans', forbidding the watering of lawns with a garden hose.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hose is played over the lawn, and its use is what drought restrictions prohibit.

clue.text: Having set off twice to fly

indicators.note: twice says the rearranged letters appear two times in a row
off means the letters of set are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Having started out two times, someone finally takes to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET into TSE, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Individuals in pubs for Lady Thatcher?

indicators.note: in places the individuals inside the pubs

parts.note: pubs are bars
individuals are single ones

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether Margaret Thatcher was found among the drinkers in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was made a life peer with the rank of baroness, so she is an example of one.

clue.text: Wine that in test appears most palatable

indicators.note: in says the wine is what sits within the word test to produce the longer word

parts.note: the most palatable food is the tastiest
the word test taken as written, whose letters are removed

explanation.surface: A wine that tastes best when put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' works backwards: the wine placed inside the word test produces 'most palatable', so the test letters are stripped out of that longer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Speechless in defeat

definitions.meaning: too moved to speak, as when emotion takes hold
to beat or get the better of an opponent

explanation.definitionFit: Being overwhelmed by feeling leaves one speechless; overwhelming an enemy is defeating them.

clue.text: Sporting side appearing in Mexico

parts.note: the Roman numeral for the number of players sits in the middle of the word Mexico

explanation.surface: A sports team turns up in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: Mexico contains the letters XI, the Roman numeral for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket teams have that many players, so the number names the team itself.

clue.text: Kind of welcome that makes us late

indicators.note: makes says these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A greeting so lengthy that it leaves us behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' tells you to rearrange US LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A salute is a gesture of greeting or welcome, as with a raised hand or gunfire.

clue.text: England's first flower festival

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word England

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: The nation's premier flower show.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian spring festival of the resurrection.

clue.text: Late back holding present, but it's heavenly

indicators.note: holding means the turned word is wrapped around the other piece
back means the word late is read backwards

parts.note: the word late taken as written
present, as in in attendance, means here

explanation.surface: Someone tardy comes back carrying a gift, and it is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LATE into ETAL, which is 'holding' HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means airy and otherworldly, as though belonging to the heavens.

clue.text: They do impressions and such for the lady

parts.note: and such means et cetera, abbreviated
something for the lady is hers

explanation.surface: Mimics and similar acts are booked for a woman's entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressions' suggests impersonators, but etchers make impressions (prints) from engraved plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchers make printed impressions from plates they have etched with acid.

clue.text: Face conceals it? The reverse, in fact

indicators.note: conceals means the first word is wrapped around the second

parts.note: to face an opponent is to oppose them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A face hides something, or rather the other way round, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'reverse' tempts a reversal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of something is its reverse, the contrary thing.

clue.text: It could be acute stress

definitions.meaning: an acute is one kind of mark over a letter, along with grave and circumflex
emphasis laid on a syllable in speech

explanation.surface: Something might be severe tension.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute is a diacritical mark, and emphasis on a syllable is the other sense of the word.

clue.text: Last miner in Cornish town works hard

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the town's name

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall

indicators.note: Last asks for the final letter of miner

explanation.surface: The last tin miner in a Cornish town toils away.
explanation.walkthrough: ST IVES is a seaside town in Cornwall, the far south-west of England, once a mining area.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make great efforts, to work hard at something.

clue.text: Take some exercise, stupid!

parts.note: to do a class is to take it
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An exasperated order to go and get some exercise, you idiot!
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid!' is used as a noun, a form of address, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is an idiot, which is what someone calls a person when shouting 'stupid!'

clue.text: They'll be beaten in time

parts.note: suggests opponents defeated eventually, but means patterns drummed out in musical tempo

explanation.surface: Rivals who will be defeated sooner or later.
explanation.definitionFit: Drummers beat out regular musical patterns, keeping to the tempo of a piece.

clue.text: Still popular stage show I've taken on

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an act is a turn in a stage show
the contraction with its apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A hit stage production that I have signed up for.
explanation.definitionFit: Being still means not moving, idle and not active.

clue.text: Suspend meeting with professional villain

parts.note: a pro is a professional
a rogue is a scoundrel or villain

explanation.surface: Halting a gathering of a paid expert and a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' looks like a noun for a gathering, but here it just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue Parliament is to suspend its sitting without dissolving it.

clue.text: Most of the side kiss and cuddle, which causes a stir!

indicators.note: Most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a sports side is a team
to spoon is old-fashioned slang for courting, kissing and cuddling

explanation.surface: Most of the team's players are caught canoodling, causing a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' suggests a scandal, but it means stirring tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon is the utensil used to stir a cup of tea.

clue.text: Net deployed by Water Board

indicators.note: deployed means the letters are spread out in a new arrangement

parts.note: rain is falling water

explanation.surface: A net is put out by the local water authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water Board' reads as a utility company, but splits: 'Water' is RAIN, 'Board' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to get on board a train.

clue.text: Bank of Scotland needs support introducing economies

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: introducing points to the opening letter of economies

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank needs backing to bring in cost-cutting measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank of Scotland' looks like the bank's name; here it means a Scottish hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a slope or hillside bank.

clue.text: Sector at sea giving protection

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naval area provides cover for shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a guard accompanying someone or something for safety.

clue.text: Girl friend takes me in on April 1st

indicators.note: takes ... in means the friend wraps round the next word
with takes, signals that one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written

indicators.note: 1st asks for the first letter of April

explanation.surface: A female friend fools me on April Fool's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes me in' suggests being fooled, fitting April Fool's Day, but 'takes ... in' is the container signal and 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamela is a girl's first name.

clue.text: A party's words softly spoken

parts.note: a side is a party to a dispute; side's gives the letters with the possessive s

explanation.surface: One faction's remarks are murmured.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks spoken quietly, as by an actor to the audience.

clue.text: Pakistan certainly hold this position

indicators.note: hold means the two words contain the run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Pakistan's government surely maintains this stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position, either physical or an attitude on an issue.

clue.text: They trouble those who lie a lot

definitions.text: They trouble those who lie a lot

parts.words: They trouble those who lie a lot
parts.note: suggests guilt bothering liars, but means sores afflicting the bedridden

explanation.surface: Something that bothers habitual fibbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients who lie in bed for long periods develop ulcers from pressure on the skin.

clue.text: Possibly old Rover's disheartened with short tail

indicators.note: disheartened means the central letter is taken out

parts.note: Rover Scouts were the old senior branch of the Scout movement, so an old Rover was a scout

explanation.surface: Perhaps an aging dog named Rover is downcast at having a stubby tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover suggests a dog, but Rovers were the senior Scouts; remove the middle O of SCOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Slimmer's chocolate ration, perhaps, if she's to look good in it!

definitions.meaning: a dieter might allow herself a single square of chocolate

definitions.text: if she's to look good in it
definitions.meaning: a swimsuit with no separate top and bottom, which a slimmer wants to look good wearing

explanation.definitionFit: A swimming costume made in a single garment is called this, as is a lone square of chocolate.

clue.text: Slow movement gets a soldier into trouble

indicators.note: into puts a soldier inside the trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A gradual advance lands a serviceman in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' suggests troops moving, but it is a section of music.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a slow movement in a piece of music.

clue.text: Server holding underwear — what a farce!

indicators.note: holding means the server wraps round the underwear

parts.note: a tray serves food and drink
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: A waiter carrying underclothes, how ridiculous!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Server' suggests a waiter, but it is the tray used for serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque mockery, a farce of what it should be.

clue.text: Oriental doesn't start at the back

indicators.note: doesn't start means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: oriental means eastern

explanation.surface: A man from the East fails to get going, staying behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word meaning at or towards the rear of a ship.
